exposure: around-the-clock (ATC) scheduled dosing of opioid analgesia
pro re nata (PRN) dosing of opioid analgesia
outcome: mean oxycodone use per inpatient day
patient satisfaction with pain control (HCAHPS scores)
cohort: Women who underwent singleton deliveries at ≥37 weeks of gestation
finding: Scheduled multimodal analgesia that includes ATC dosing of acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and low-dose oxycodone after cesarean delivery does not increase oxycodone use compared to as-needed analgesia, while it increases the percentage of women receiving oxycodone after vaginal delivery, but does not change the mean oxycodone consumption.
mod_finding: The study investigated a scheduled multimodal analgesic regimen compared to as-needed analgesia for postpartum pain management, finding no increase in oxycodone use after cesarean deliveries but an increase in the percentage of women receiving oxycodone after vaginal deliveries with the scheduled approach.
